title: Why Coins Have Ridges, Manholes Are Round and Stop Signs Have 8 Sides
description:
In 1696, a man with a pair of scissors could be hanged for what he did to a silver coin. The man sent to stop him was Isaac Newton, and his answer is still in your pocket today.

Almost every strange shape around you was a fix for a real problem. Why do coins have ridged edges? Why are manhole covers round? Why do stop signs have 8 sides, and why were they yellow for 30 years? Why do paper bags have flat bottoms, bottle caps exactly 21 teeth, plug prongs little holes, and crackers rows of holes? Each one has a person, a place and a year behind it.

Chapters
0:00 Isaac Newton vs the coin clippers
0:34 Why coins have ridges

2:51 Why paper bags have flat bottoms
3:34 Why bottle caps have 21 teeth
4:17 Why plug prongs have holes
4:55 Why crackers have holes
5:30 None of these shapes are an accident
